I will keep my land in the winter wheat and summer maize rotation. In Quzhou, that is the cropping pattern I trust most because the seed, machines, irrigation habits, and grain buyers all match it, and I can manage it well without taking market risk on a more delicate cash crop. I will run 10 mu on one rotation: the wheat is already the standing crop for this season, and after harvest I will go straight into summer maize. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed, keep fertilizer moderate instead of chasing the very highest input level, irrigate at the key stages, return straw, and stay on a simple spray schedule. For wheat, I will focus water and nitrogen around jointing and booting, with one herbicide pass and one fungicide/insecticide pass. For maize, I will direct-seed after wheat harvest, use no-tillage into the stubble, feed it mainly around the big flare stage, irrigate for emergence and grain filling if needed, and keep sprays to weed control plus one later protection pass. I’m basing this on the local Quzhou winter wheat-summer maize system documented by China Agricultural University’s Quzhou station and Ministry of Agriculture guidance for the North China Plain: https://news.cau.edu.cn/zhxwnew/ff0f90c1f75b4d04ab700a67a30086d5.htm, https://www.moa.gov.cn/gk/nszd_1/2023/202309/t20230928_6437567.htm, https://www.moa.gov.cn/xw/qg/202411/t20241104_6465572.htm, https://www.moa.gov.cn/xw/qg/202406/t20240617_6457244.htm
